Maintainer risk: MEDIUM — code is clean and tests pass, but the public _set/_get/_query/_queryChanges builders ship without standard RFC 8620 args (ifInState, anchor, anchorOffset, calculateTotal, upToId) and without a vendor-extras escape hatch. Those signatures are about to fossilise into 0.1.0 across the extension-client family; fixing later is a breaking change.
Confidence: ~85% chance of no missed bug. Least confident flags: none of the Section 0 (correctness) section had findings, so the calibration is mainly about whether I missed a wire-format bug in the JSON serialisation of one of the five method builders. I read all five builders end-to-end and the wiremock tests do exercise the full round-trip. Uncertainty driven by: (a) I did not run the metadata-server <-> metadata-client integration with anything other than wiremock — the existing tests do not pair the two real implementations and check that what one sends is what the other expects (this is a gap in workspace test coverage, not in this crate); (b) I read draft-ietf-jmap-metadata-01 §3 in full but did not read §4 (Standard Method Extensions on existing data types like Email/get + metadata args) which the crate's PLAN.md explicitly says are out of scope for this crate; (c) I did not exhaust the comparator/filter algebra side of /query, only confirmed the spec lets filter pass through as Value. Would raise confidence if: a real client-server integration test pairing jmap-metadata-server::handle_metadata_* with metadata_* method builders existed; would raise confidence further if a fuzz/property test asserted that every (Params, args) combination's wire shape matches one of the spec's example shapes.
API contract risk: MEDIUM — five fields/structs ship in 0.1.0 with shape commitments that are cheap to fix now and breaking to fix after: metadata_get has no params slot (wzq9.14), MetadataChangesParams is not #[non_exhaustive] (wzq9.15), error-cause is string-encoded (wzq9.16), upstream re-exports lock major version (wzq9.21), and several docs gaps describe inputs by spec reference only (wzq9.23, wzq9.24). Most findings have a workspace-wide propagation footprint via the canonical mail-client; fixing here only is half the work.
API contract confidence: ~80% chance of no missed issue. Least confident flags: (a) wzq9.18 (extras silent-collision semantics) — I asserted Map::entry/or_insert is no-op on existing key but did not write a wiremock test to confirm the wire shape when extras and typed fields share a key. The code reading is correct but the unit-test coverage for that specific path is absent. (b) Did not exhaustively check whether every existing public type (Annotation, ImapMetadata, WebDavMetadata via re-export from jmap-metadata-types) is itself #[non_exhaustive] — that's a jmap-metadata-types concern that crosses crate boundaries from this review's scope. (c) Did not survey the canonical mail-client to confirm that every finding I labelled 'workspace-wide propagation' is actually identical in shape on canonical-side. Uncertainty driven by: review scope is one crate (metadata-client) but most findings have workspace-wide footprint; the propagation half is not in scope here and was not verified beyond a one-file grep.
Idiom rating: CLEAN — crate is a faithful cookie-cut of canonical jmap-mail-client; matches the deliberate .expect-vs-.map_err split for serde_json::to_value, the imperative json!({...}) args-envelope, the #[non_exhaustive]+pub(crate)-fields SessionClient shape, the Jmap<Ext>Ext::with_<ext>_session extension-trait pattern, and the pub(crate) const CALL_ID/USING_* constants. Two clippy-level idiom nits filed (wzq9.27 loop-invariant hoist, wzq9.28 let-else in test) — neither is a soundness or design concern, both are stylistic improvements.

API contract risk (supplement pass 3): MEDIUM — supplement pass against current HEAD (d0a0bd4). One new finding filed (wzq9.35, P2, api-contract+docs): the # Errors rustdoc section on metadata_set added in d0a0bd4 contains a factually wrong claim that the wire request is 'streamed by the HTTP client' — actually buffered upfront via reqwest::RequestBuilder::json -> serde_json::to_vec, producing a transient 3-4x peak memory profile rather than the streamed shape callers will infer. Engineering basis: callers sizing update HashMaps against the wrong memory model will OOM at to_vec/json() rather than midway through a streamed send; the recommended-batching advice in the same doc is right for the wrong stated reason. MEDIUM verdict unchanged from prior supplement pass; the substantive immutability/leakage/versioning/defensive/underspecified gaps remain tracked by wzq9.{1,2,14,15,16,17,19,20,21,22,25,29,30,31,32,33,34} as before. The exact ratio could be off by a small factor but the qualitative claim (buffered, not streamed) is correct.
